---
title: "Computerized adaptive testing"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 110)
library(IRTistic)
set.seed(7)
```

An adaptive test chooses each item to be as informative as possible about
the person taking it, so it reaches a target precision with far fewer items
than a fixed form (Weiss, 1982). IRTistic covers the full workflow, taking
ideas and defaults from catR (Magis & Barrada, 2017) and mirtCAT (Chalmers,
2016).

## 1. An item bank

Use calibrated items from `item_bank(fit)` or published parameters from
`make_bank()`. Content areas are optional.

```{r}
bank <- make_bank(b = rnorm(300), a = rlnorm(300, 0.1, 0.3), model = "2pl",
                  content = sample(c("Algebra", "Geometry", "Number"), 300, replace = TRUE))
bank
```

## 2. A design

```{r}
design <- cat_design(bank, select = "MFI", estimator = "EAP",
                     min_items = 5, max_items = 30, se_target = 0.30,
                     exposure = "randomesque", randomesque_k = 5,
                     content_target = c(Algebra = 0.4, Geometry = 0.3, Number = 0.3))
design
```

Selection rules: maximum Fisher information (`"MFI"`), posterior-weighted
information (`"MPWI"`), Kullback-Leibler (`"KL"`), minimum expected posterior
variance (`"MEPV"`) and `"random"`. Exposure control: randomesque,
Sympson-Hetter (`cat_sympson_hetter()` calibrates the parameters) and
a-stratification (`strata =`). Stopping rules: test length, SE target and
classification against cut scores (`cut =`).

## 3. Running it live

`cat_start()`, `cat_next()` and `cat_answer()` give the item-by-item loop
behind a web form or a 'shiny' app.

```{r}
s <- cat_start(design)
true_theta <- 0.8
while (!cat_done(s)) {
  item <- cat_next(s)
  p <- 1 / (1 + exp(-bank$items[[item]]$a * (true_theta + bank$items[[item]]$d / bank$items[[item]]$a)))
  s <- cat_answer(s, item, rbinom(1, 1, p))
}
s
plot(s)
```

## 4. Simulation studies

```{r}
sim <- cat_simulate(design, theta = rnorm(500), seed = 1)
summary(sim)
irt_table(sim)
```

```{r, fig.height = 5}
plot(sim, "conditional")
plot(sim, "exposure", r_max = 0.25)
```

## 5. Classification testing

```{r}
pass_fail <- cat_design(bank, cut = 0.5, min_items = 8, max_items = 40)
cls <- cat_simulate(pass_fail, theta = rnorm(300), seed = 2)
summary(cls)
plot(cls, "trace", person = 3)
```

## 6. Post-hoc simulation with real data

Pass a complete response matrix instead of `theta` to find out how short an
adaptive version of an existing test could be.

```{r}
dat <- sim_irt(400, 40, "grm", ncat = 4)
fit <- irt_fit(dat, "grm", se = "none")
ph <- cat_simulate(cat_design(fit, max_items = 15, se_target = 0.35), responses = as.matrix(dat))
summary(ph)
cor(ph$results$theta, irt_scores(fit)$theta)   # agreement with the full 40-item test
```
